//: FRONTEND-BFF.md §7 — a member of the workspace above, which owns the only lockfile.
THIS IS THE SECOND APP, and the root package.json used to say what that would
trigger: '@ab-ovo/web-kit ... is created when the SECOND app arrives.' It has been
created — see web/web-kit/package.json — and the loader crossing this package made
(src/content.ts, gone with the bundle in #171) was redirected to it in the same commit,
exactly the 'one import to redirect rather than a search' its own header predicted. See
docs/architecture/MCP-SERVER-SKETCH.md §6, updated alongside this file rather than left
describing a trigger that already fired.
One runtime dependency: the MCP SDK. @ab-ovo/web-kit is a DEVELOPMENT dependency, and
that is deliberate (#172): it is a private workspace package no registry has, so it
cannot be a dependency of anything a registry installs. The server takes the reading
order (isOpenWhere), the grouping and adjacency of a track's programs, and the content
API's wire shapes from it, and scripts/build.ts carries the modules it uses into dist/
beside the server's own, so an installed package needs nothing from the workspace.
Since #171 this server is a client of AbOvo.Api (ADR-0066 §1): the book, the reveal gate
and the reader's place are the API's, reached by src/api.ts over the global fetch, and
nothing here loads a bundle — no book, no fetch script and no compiler are needed to
run it, only AB_OVO_API_URL. The unit tier runs against a stub of the API
(src/testing/stub-api.ts), which serves it the committed fixture.
name: @ab-ovo/mcp
description: An MCP server that serves a programmed-learning book one step at a time, as a client of an ab-ovo API. It carries no book.
//name: THE PACKAGE'S NAME IS THE OWNER'S TO CHOOSE (#172, ADR-0070), and this field is the one
place it is set: the launcher's --version and --help, the tarball's file name and every
`npx` command a README gives are read from or written against it. `@ab-ovo/mcp` is the
workspace's name for the package, which no one has registered with npm and which may not
be the owner's to publish under — a scope on npm belongs to an account. The server's own
name in the MCP handshake is `ab-ovo` and is not this field.
docs/how-to/publish-the-mcp-package.md is the checklist that sets it.
//private: `private: true` STAYS UNTIL THE OWNER'S FIRST PUBLISH, and removing it is a step of that
checklist and not of this issue (ADR-0070). npm refuses to publish a private package, so
until a person removes the line no command run by accident — `pnpm -r publish`, an
`npm publish` in the wrong directory — can make a version public under a name nobody
chose, and a version number once published cannot be used again (ADR-0066 §3). Packing is
not publishing: `pnpm pack` makes the tarball of a private package, which is all CI
needs. The flip is one commit that also sets `name`, so what the owner publishes is a
revision the history shows them choosing.
//license: MIT covers the code. The book is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, is not in the package (ADR-0033,
ADR-0066 §4), and is credited where the server's prose reaches a reader (src/credit.ts).
//repository: The repository is `ab-ove` today and the rename to `ab-ovo` is coming (ADR-0005, #78).
GitHub redirects the old address, but npm's trusted publishing compares this URL with the
repository a workflow runs in (ADR-0070), so it is edited in the commit that renames.
//bin: The launcher an MCP host is pointed at. Plain JavaScript on purpose: it checks the Node
version BEFORE importing the server, because the Node that cannot strip types cannot
parse src/server.ts to be told so. It runs src/ in a checkout and dist/ in the package
(its own header says how it tells them apart). `pnpm start` goes through it too, so the
one path a developer tries is the one a host uses.
//files: WHAT THE TARBALL CARRIES, AND NOTHING ELSE (#172). The launcher, the compiled server in
dist/, the licence and the README (npm adds package.json itself). NOT src/, which is
TypeScript Node would not strip under node_modules; NOT scripts/, the tests or the
stub API; and NO BOOK — the book is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and is not redistributed through npm
(ADR-0033, ADR-0066 §4). scripts/build.ts writes dist/ and refuses to carry a file under
web/content/ but the pin, and scripts/verify-tarball.ts refuses a tarball with a file it
does not recognise. LICENSE is the repository's, copied in by the build; both it and
dist/ are output and are gitignored.
//publishConfig: A scoped package is published restricted unless it is told otherwise, and this one is
free (ADR-0066 §4). An unscoped name is unaffected. No `provenance` here: that is for
a publish from CI, and ADR-0070 says when that is turned on.

//test: Same unit tier as @ab-ovo/app: node --test runs .ts directly through Node 22's type
stripping, so this adds no runner and no transform. Wired into ci.yml in the same
//lint: THERE IS DELIBERATELY NO lint SCRIPT. pnpm -r skips a member that does not declare
one, and a script that echoes instead of linting is the defect TESTING-STRATEGY.md
§9 names for test entry points -- documentation that lies, green forever, proving
nothing. @ab-ovo/app lints through eslint-config-next, which is Next's and not this
package's; a flat config of its own is a follow-up with its own dependency decision.
//build: dist/ and LICENSE, from the source: what the tarball carries beside the launcher.
`prepack` is the same step, so `pnpm pack` and `npm publish` can never package a dist/
older than the source; .github/workflows/mcp-package.yml runs it that way.
